chapter: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
title: Willie the Lion Smith walks out and Barefield takes over the Streetcar band
summary: A fight between Willie and George Avakian made Willie quit, leaving Barefield as leader at scale. He recruited Dick Vance and a drummer and tried several stride pianists before Johnny Mehegan was chosen.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Okay. Now, you say George Avakian took it over.

Yeah. And so Willie the Lion Smith, he got him to be the leader. So anyway, so now Willie calls me and wants me to do it with him. I said okay. So now they're going to do it for scale, for union scale. All right.

So they come to my office on 48th Street to make a rehearsal. And in rehearsal Willie and George got into -- George Avakian -- got into a fight. And Willie walked out. So he ran on out, and George followed him out. Five minutes later George came back, says, Willie's quit. Would you take it? I said okay.
So now I'm from $1,000.00 a week down to the scale, right?

Well, the director's scale, you know, I'll get probable double -- I'll get double for the -- and what the men get. So anyway, I took it. And we needed a piano player. See, we had -- we had Dick Vance and myself. I got Dick Vance, and we had a little drummer named Kenny --
oh -- he came here with Dick Wellstood Wilsted. Strong, Den Strong -- Dennis Strong. I don't know if you ever heard, but he came down from Scarsdale with the Dick- Bob Wilburn --

Yeah, and Dick Wellstood and all of them. But Dennis Strong, he was the drummer, and we needed a piano player. So now they wanted -- asked me to get a piano soprano. So I thought, oh, I'll call -- the fellow that married Maxine Sullivan Sawburn.

Cliff Jackson came down and, oh, I had Cliff Jackson, and I can give you a name of all the stride piano players that they were looking for to come down there, and they weren't satisfied with any of them. So I just said, well, forget it. You get somebody.

So they come up with Johnny Mehegan. So now we -- we got a trumpet, clarinet, drums and piano. So we go into rehearsal for the show. Now, the -- so now, Maheema Nigrel was the musical director. He didn't know anything about jazz or what it was supposed to do, says, Barefield, it's up to you.
